utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number of the case is IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution. I would like to greet Mr. Withopf, who is amongst us yet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Kyle Wood, Ekkehard Withopf, and Ruth Karper, the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And the appearances for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Muriel Cauvin, our legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone present in the courtroom, members of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, and everyone else present here. We'll continue with the cross-examination of the witness today. Both Defence teams will conduct this cross-examination. The Trial Chamber would like to point out that as we have already said, it's necessary to conclude the cross-examination today. In theory, Mr. Bourgon has between an hour and a half and two hours for his cross-examination, and this should allow Defence for Mr. Kubura to conduct their examination for the two hours that they have requested, unless Mr. Dixon would like to inform us that he requires less time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes. Good morning, Your Honours. We do require less time. And we've spoken to Mr. Bourgon about this, and the proposal that we therefore have for the division of time today is to allow Mr. Bourgon to continue for the first session, until 10.30, and then when we usually resume at five to 11.00, if -- if he be permitted to continue from then until 12.00, for a further hour, and at that stage, if we could request that we have our break until twenty-five past 12.00, and then I will commence the cross-examination for Mr. Kubura at that stage, estimating that it will take about an hour or just over an hour. That will allow the cross-examination to be done in one continuous flow and also will allow us to set up a -- a videotape, because we have a small piece of video to show the witness and Your Honours during his testimony. And that could be done in the break. So if that is convenient for Your Honours, we'd propose that as a division of time today and then the Defence cross-examination will be finished at the end of today. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This plan is perfect and fits into the plan we've already established. Without wasting any more time, I would like to ask the usher to call the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General. I'd first like to check that you're receiving interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would also like to check that the documents that you were promised yesterday were provided to you in the course of yesterday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir, they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Bourgon, you may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Madam Judge. Good morning, Your Honour. Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Bourgon: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, General. Once again, thank you for being here this morning. And I shall proceed with my last segment of the cross-examination today, in reference to and in relation to your expert report as filed previously before this Chamber. What I would like to do to begin with, General, of course you have been given some -- you have been given three different documents yesterday at the end of the afternoon, along with some questions that I would like to put to you a little later today towards the end of my cross-examination. For now I would like to simply come back quickly on the issue of the measures that had been taken by the accused General Enver Hadzihasanovic while he was commanding general of the 3rd Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. General, would I be right in saying that as you were drafting this report and as part of the questions which were asked of you by the Prosecution the measures or the lack thereof taken by General Hadzihasanovic was one of the main focuses of what you were asked to look at?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was one of the focuses I was asked to look at, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And may I confirm with you, General, this morning that at some point during the cross-examination you mentioned that as you were looking throughout all these documents that were provided to you by the Prosecution you were basically surprised at to what extent the documents displayed a will on the part of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina from its president, Mr. Izetbegovic, down to the 3rd Corps and its subordinate units that the operations be conducted in accordance with the law?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you could see this from the -- from the multiple documents that you reviewed.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in your report, you also mentioned that General Hadzihasanovic did issue a number of reports -- a number of orders, sorry, with a view to preventing violations from being committed.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was also your view that General Hadzihasanovic felt responsible for the prevention of such violations.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He, I think, went even further; he basically declared that the new Bosnian army should not fight the same way as their opponents would fight. He was claiming for a more human way of fighting according to the international law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in some cases, at least one of which is reported in your expert report, you mentioned that General Hadzihasanovic did exactly what could be expected of a commanding general being faced with allegations, in terms of doing the right thing from the investigation down until we have results.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I stated this is unfortunately the only case I found in the document. This is the Kakanj case, where he basically sent the military police, he investigated, and he gave a clear order then to the commander -- the commander of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade to relieve some of the officers he thought that they would be -- they hadn't done the job properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And yesterday, General, we went through some of the documents when we were discussing measures, and one of the cases we discussed was the investigation which was triggered by General Hadzihasanovic in relation to some events in Susanj, where some 19 people had died. Do you recall us discussing this issue yesterday?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you confirm that what you mentioned yesterday was that the way this situation was handled was exactly what could be expected of a commanding general in a position of General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the things that you did mention is that although some orders had been issued by General Hadzihasanovic, you pointed out in your report that the orders seemed to have been timely, in terms of close after some events, which would, in your opinion, show that he had a certain knowledge of something bad had taken place; he was willing to try and tell his soldiers not to do it again, if that was the case; but at the same time, that it did not appear to you that he did take actions to punish.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at least I didn't find anything in the documents which would lead me to that conclusion, and that was the problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when we talk about taking measures, General, I'd like to confirm with you that of course one of the measures which can be taken is punishment. You would agree with me that this is probably the most typical type of measure?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you also agree with me, General, that other measures can be taken to ensure that violations are not repeated and to ensure that the troops are under control?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is too global. I don't want to answer on this, because I don't know what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will give you maybe some examples. By training your soldiers, you can, on one hand, prevent and ensure that the soldiers and the leadership of your corps is able to stop violations from being committed.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, sir. This is a preventive measure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By -- once you learn of your enemy committing serious violations or acting beyond the law - and we discussed yesterday the impact that this can have on your own army - that protests, I suggest to you, could be a valid way of ensuring that crimes don't happen again.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The protest to the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say that for a commanding general, especially in the present situation, to propose a meeting with the opponent to discuss such issues would also be a good way for both armies to conduct or to wage warfare in accordance with the law?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you understood from your reading of the documents that were provided to you that at least until January of 1993 the HVO and the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were meant and for all intents and purposes were supposed to fight together.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were basically on the same side fighting against the Army of Republika Srpska, the VRS.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that it is in the course of 1993 that this situation changed radically.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that a former ally turned its back on General Hadzihasanovic and that that complicated the situation very much.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you could understand from the documents that were shown to you that not only he had now two enemies or two front lines, but that in fact one of those enemies was within his own lines.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As soon as a general learns of an issue or some type of violation, you would agree with me that investigating or at least seeking information should be the way to go?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as we discussed yesterday, the reliability of the information is important and in the absence of any indication to the contrary a commanding general must trust the information he receives.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you also agree with me that having a proper legal department or at least trying to have a proper legal department would also be a good way to ensure that the law would be respected?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. The legal department and the security forces, I would say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So both military police doing their job and the legal department.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, both depend on the quality of the people that you will get, not quality in terms of subjective quality but whether these people are trained to do their jobs; would you agree?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we have international observers in the area and these international observers offer their assistance with a view to allowing investigations of complaints by either side, would you agree with me that cooperation with such a commission would indeed be also a good way to find out what happened -- what happens on the ground and to be able to react to these complaints?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This would also allow a commanding general in many respects to determine whether such complaints are founded or whether such complaints sometimes are ill-founded.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in your own experience in Kosovo, it is my understanding that there were such type of commissions. Could you elaborate on your own experience and the use of the commissions in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- during my tenure, we had none of those commissions; but in my tenure, we had a lot of accusations of either side claiming the other side of war criminal activities. So for every Serb, a UCK fighter, by being a guy like this, was a terrorist and a criminal because he fought against his own state. While for the Albanians, every young Serb who has joined the army as a draftee became a war criminal as long as he fought within Kosovo, because these were the guys who committed the crimes. And there was this mutual accusation but not very substantiated, and we tried to find evidence on the individual cases in order to look for that, but it was very difficult, but there was not an official commission looking for that. I think this was the evidence which in the -- in the individual areas of responsibility of the nations, the nations - like the Dutch, like the British, like the Germans - tried to find out with their legal capabilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I've -- I've had a look, of course, in the documentation which was provided to you, and correct me if I'm wrong but you received little information on the Busovaca joint commission.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't ring a bell, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you had been made aware that there was such a thing as the Busovaca joint commission, which was composed of three people from the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and three representatives from the HVO and at the highest level - for example, I think it is in the documentation in some area that the deputy commander to General Hadzihasanovic was a member of this commission -

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Merdan?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Merdan. And that Mr. Nakic, if you are familiar with the name, was the deputy commander of Blaskic, who -- on the HVO, and that they were both on this commission and they often travelled together to try and substantiate complaints that the commission had received. Would you say that this type of commission and this type of endeavour by a commanding general by participating fully in such a commission, that he is indeed trying to find out and do the necessary fact-finding to ensure that violations are not committed?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the information that you were provided, General, correct me if I'm wrong, but you did not get much information, if any, on the efforts of both parties to establish a joint command or a joint headquarters.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you say, General, that for these two armies who were former allies, who were now fighting each other, the will at the highest level, at the army level, to establish such a joint command would also be a good way to prevent violations but also to ensure that they are stopped?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be a possibility, but I think this somehow surpasses my capability, because the key question you're asking right now is a political and not a military question. As long as the two political parties are not willing to form a joint headquarters, the different armies cannot do this. So it's -- it's one of the key political questions which arose by that time, and I'm not willing to comment on that because I have no capability of doing that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Are you familiar from the documentation that you have read with the names General Petkovic on behalf of the HVO, and General Halilovic, on behalf of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with the name of General Halilovic. I think I also read about General Petkovic, but I have no clear information on him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I was to tell you, General, that these two generals at the highest level established or signed a joint order to establish a joint command, which then led to Colonel Blaskic, from the HVO, and General Hadzihasanovic to also sign a series of orders in January, to establish not only this joint headquarters but also to take steps to release prisoners, to remove checkpoints, to pick up the bodies, and a couple of other things, and of course to participate in joint fact-finding operations, would that also be a good way for a commanding general to accomplish his duty as the conduct of law -- conduct of waging of war within the parameters of the law?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I read about the cooperation of General Hadzihasanovic and Colonel Blaskic, and I think this was a very clever way to do business, to try to overcome some of the problems in which both army were at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I would like to do at this time, General, is to talk a bit about the situation in which both armies were.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the situation in the context in which General Hadzihasanovic operated and exercised his command. We -- you confirmed yesterday the importance of various aspects of the context and of the situation. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That many factors could have an impact on the ability of General Hadzihasanovic to exercise his command and in some cases to take decisions, depending on the time.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at this point in time the Defence would like to do the following: I'd like to use the maps that are behind the witness, and with your leave, Mr. President, I would like to approach the map in order to point to certain locations. I have already discussed this with my colleague from the Prosecution, in order to inform -- I wanted to inform my colleague that I intended to use these maps. As I point to certain locations on the map, I would be in a position to say where the maps come from and what the Defence's intention is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... go towards the map and simple life highlight some issues for you. And given that I do not need the listening device, then I guess I will be able to show you some of the areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm not sure whether the microphone is working. Mr. President, I would first of all like to use one of the maps here. I have asked one of the technicians if it would be possible to direct the camera here and to have map number 1 on the screen. Could we have a close-up of map number 1. We've tested this. It was working earlier on. Mr. President, Your Honours, I don't know whether you can see things clearly. The "1" has been reversed, given the time at which this number was written down, but this is map number 1. Mr. President, this is a map which comes from the headquarters of the UNPROFOR command. The date of the map is the 6th of June, 1993. We're dealing with parts of this map, Mr. President, and we will obtain a copy of this map. We have made such a request, which has been addressed to the United Nations, but we haven't received the map yet. Nevertheless, my colleague has agreed to me using this map for the purposes of Mr. Reinhardt's testimony.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... areas, and of course, as we normally do it for intelligence briefing, I will start from the more broader picture, moving down to the more specific. So I will be following from map number 1, to map number 2, to map number 3, which illustrate the same area at various points in time, and then move down to the more specific, which is the larger map which is here, which is map number 4. Map number 4 --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I forgot to mention the fourth map, which is a map used in the headquarters of General Hadzihasanovic. The instructions on the name of the map is here. It's a 3rd Corps map. It's divided on the basis of operational groups. And the date is August 1993. We've covered this map with transparent plastic and we have added certain details to make it clearer and more visible. I have informed my colleague from the Prosecution how we can proceed, and at a subsequent date we intend to present the original map, which is the map that General Hadzihasanovic had in his headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... to go to map number 1 and to basically, first of all, show you the area of the 3rd Corps as you have seen it from the documents. And what is important is that you see the area - and I will go slowly so that the camera can follow me - and this here is the area covered by the 3rd Corps. And we recognise Zenica as being where the headquarters of the 3rd Corps was, and we recognise the cities you are probably familiar with from the documents you have seen, which is Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca, and then Kakanj. So this is -- and Bugojno is also part, and Gornji Vakuf, in terms of the area of the 3rd Corps. What I would like to bring your attention on is the situation that is taking place here, first of all with Sarajevo, because you have seen the documents illustrating that immediately from the beginning of the war the -- Sarajevo was encircled, there was a siege, and it was very difficult, if at all possible, for anyone to come into Sarajevo. The other thing I would like to mention to you is to show you this place here, which is Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gorazde, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Gorazde is not in the area of the 3rd Corps; however, what I would like to point out is the area leading to Gorazde, this area here. We see a dotted line. Now, the dotted line refers to - and we can't see it because it is hidden - but the dotted line refers to internal confrontation lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. My learned colleague in fact did discuss the use of these maps and what use was going to be put to the maps with the Prosecution yesterday. I rise to my feet because our objection at this point is that my learned colleague is not putting questions to the witness but, in our respectful view, has -- has perhaps crossed into the line of -- of testifying himself, with respect to the detail that he is providing to the expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this stage, the Chamber takes note of the observations of the Defence, who is indicating to the witness the area covered by the 3rd Corps, the towns of Travnik, Zenica, and the other towns. He mentioned Sarajevo, in order to present all the elements that would lead up to the question. Is that right, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the understanding of the Chamber as well. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... this area, can you confirm that you recognise the area that you have been -- that you have been reading about as being the area of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part which you just described is the area of the 3rd Corps, but I'm a little bit mixed up right now. Is the red -- thick red line the area within the 3rd Corps operated?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, would you -- I would put this, rather, as being a question to you, in terms of this red line here is actually the line of confrontation.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I thought. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That being the line of confrontation, General, on this side - inside, of course, we would find - I'm trying not to testify to follow what my colleague is saying, but am I right in saying that the HVO and the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina would have been holding this front line?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that on the other side of the front line would have been the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to the area of Maglaj. Can you explain on the basis of your knowledge and your professional expertise how would you describe this area from Maglaj, Tesanj, and Doboj.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's a -- a very mountainous area, a difficult area to operate in, broken terrain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will -- General, I understand that this is -- my questions are not very precise, because I'm trying not to testify, but what I would like to draw your attention to is, in terms of the confrontation line, if you were a -- the opposing military and if you were the Army of Republika Srpska, what would you attempt to do with this area here?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the whole area is full of pockets, and -- and you would like to try to consolidate your -- your area of Defence or your defensive lines or your FEBA, whatever you would call it in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, on this particular map, we cannot see the roads, but on a further map we will be able to see the roads. But you can confirm, General, that the issue of roads is indeed a very important issue for the commanding general?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is for the commanding general. This was also for the future, I think, of Bosnia-Herzegovina, because this is Central Bosnia, and who keeps the roads is the master of the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I would like to move now to map number 2. Map number 2 is further in time. And I would like you to describe, General, what you see from the same area of Maglaj, Tesanj, and Doboj, in terms of what has happened here with this dotted line being an internal line of confrontation.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot tell you what happened here. I don't know. I cannot -- I cannot -- it looks with -- if I see 2 Bravo, there were two attempts closing the whole pocket around Srebrenica and Tuzla to the south, because at 2 Charlie you also have an arrow in the south, in order to cut off the whole north-eastern part of that pocket and probably also the area south of Maglaj, but this is just an hypothesis which I deduct from the way this map has been drawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, would I be right if I asked you to compare the issue of Gorazde and the issue of Gorazde here --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: May I have a close-up, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was Gorazde in June, the 6th of June. And I slowly move up to the next map, also asking for a close-up. And what has happened to the same area in a matter of weeks -- sorry, Gorazde is here.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having been to Gorazde, having seen the terrible destruction of the city and the area around, it shows here that by the time of the two time lines we are discussing, Gorazde has been cut off from the Bosnian area; it has been under siege; and it was a very difficult way because there was no additional connection between the -- the forces defending the centre area of Bosnia and the forces in Gorazde. They were cut off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I would now like to move to the third map and refer to the area of Tesanj, Doboj, and Maglaj that we were referring to. And I note that this map is dated the 18th of July, 1993. May I have a close-up, please, to show what has happened to the area of Doboj, Tesanj, and Maglaj. If I can -- if I ask you, General, to comment on this situation, as compared to map number 1, map number 2, and map number 3.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, it shows that the area of Tesanj in the north has been cut off from the main area of defence. It also shows that the -- the attempt to cut off the north-eastern part, which we have saw here by those arrows, didn't seem to be successful. So additional individual pockets of resistance which made it very difficult for a coherent operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I ask you to comment, General, on the situation, in terms of the lost ground for the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which no longer has access to this pocket, how would you comment on the consequences?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two consequences: One consequence is to give up the area, clean it up and consolidate your forces; the other possibility is to try to re-establish contact. By all means, if it's so important for you, I don't know whether this area was very important from the point of view of the operations, but I think these are the basic possibilities which you have under conditions like this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, before we move on to map number 4, I would like you to comment on, if you look at map number 1, inside the territory that you have identified as being that of the 3rd Corps, and if we move to this second map with the same area, and if I move to the third map with the same area, can you comment on what you see inside the territory.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the General -- would the General please speak into the microphone. The interpreters cannot hear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You caught me cold here, and I don't -- how does it work?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I'm sorry. You caught me cold here, because I haven't seen this map before. But the way I read it, it shows that HVO forces are within the corps area, so there is an internal fight in all these areas about probably key terrain for the defence of the 3rd Corps. So it's a fight outside -- or it -- at the outside against an enemy who tries to condense this, and it's a fight against enemy which is inside your area of operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We will now move to the larger map, and the larger map being the one I indicated from the 3rd Corps. What I would like to ask you to -- whether you recognise this line with the military symbol that is being used, what would this be?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the corps boundary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you recognise this area inside as being the area of which corps?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It seems that this is the area of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the colour of the lines which are being used here, just for your information - and I point down to the legend at the bottom of the map - I don't know if it is possible to have a close-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can we have a close-up, please, on the legend of the map here down?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The legend here indicates that the lines in blue are that of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that the lines in red are that of the VRS, and that the lines in orange are that of the HVO. What I have added to this map in a different colour than the original is the black lines, which illustrate the roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: May I have a close-up here, and if you can please follow me simply to indicate you the roads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then I will, General, ask you a question about the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Could I have a close-up -- yes. I will try to indicate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The town that you see here is Zavidovici, and I would simply drive down this road and show you exactly the importance of that road, and the road goes here. This is the road that leads to Zenica and the corps headquarters. Basically it is a road leading up north that was leading before to the area that we saw, the pocket that has been taken over by the VRS. Now, from Zenica here -- I understand it appears to be a bit difficult with the camera -- to have access to Sarajevo, it was necessary to drive this road here, and I follow slowly with the pointer, driving through an area called, of course, Kakanj, and then we come to a junction here. The junction is a two-way; you either go left, and you see how difficult it is to go around; and all the way down around the boundary of where the HVO is, in orange, taking the road all the way around to Sarajevo. The other road here at this crossroad is the one that leads up north. And if I follow slowly this road going up north, it goes -- crosses the corps boundary that you have identified and goes up north, leading all the way down -- up to Tuzla. My question, General, is as follows: If you look at this area here, the road to Sarajevo, how would you describe, because of the orange line here and here, what happens if the general loses this territory between these two -- between these two orange pockets?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, we see that the corps had to fight, with inverted lines, in two different directions; very, very difficult. And it had to rely on those roads of communications by all means. And it's rather obvious from the disposition of the HVO forces that they tried to cut off this road. I know the road, because I've driven that, and we have reinforced this road later in the southern part. It's a very, very difficult road to negotiate. It goes over high mountainous terrain. It's not a road which we normally would consider a road like a paved road, so this was a very, very difficult line of communications from the 3rd Corps across the mountains into the Sarajevo area, key, I think, for any kind of communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. One last question with this -- the upper part of the map. If I can have a close-up. We see the town here which is the town of -- and I'm looking for Vares, which is right here. This is Vares. And so would you confirm, General, that Vares here is not in the same corps area as the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Vares is in the -- as far as I remember, in the 6th Corps area, and -- but for forces of the 3rd Corps were linked to the neighbouring corps in order to reinforce them for operations in Vares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, by looking at the red line, in terms of the line of confrontation, what would be the result if the line of confrontation that is here, close to Vares, and the line of confrontation that is here, this is the pocket that was just been taken, if we close this gap and we lose this terrain in Vares, what happens -- or what is the result for the commanding general?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would have been cut off from his neighbouring corps. He would have -- and the neighbouring corps would have lost a key area, as far as a strategic turntable -- traffic turntable is concerned. So it was of utmost importance also for the 3rd Corps, rather than only the neighbouring corps, to keep Vares and to keep this corridor open.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I indicate to you, General, that this is the only road up north leading to Tuzla, which we do not see on this map, would I be right in saying that be closing the gap between Zepce and Vares it would be no longer -- it would be completely cut off from the road and not able to drive any more to Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I just tried to explain before. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would simply like to go back on the bigger picture and simply show -- to have three snapshots so that we can see the difference. The first snapshot is this one here. I would like to have a close-up. And we see the pocket here between Maglaj, Tesanj, and Doboj. Now, this is the first snapshot. Now, at the same time we see the difference between Vares and this tip of the confrontation line, and we see that this is a very short distance between the two. In the second -- in the second snapshot, we see that battle is taking place and that there is now a new line of confrontation and that the 3rd Corps is about to lose the pocket of Maglaj, Tesanj, Doboj, and that in the Zepce area. In the third snapshot, we see that by July the pocket, Maglaj, Tesanj, Doboj, has been lost to the 3rd Corps. We now have a new pocket here of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And at the same time, the area between Vares and this tip of the confrontation line is reducing. On the basis of these three snapshots, General, can you confirm that what would be the focus of the general's attention of an operational perspective at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the third thing which you just described I cannot deduct from the map, because I think the distance from Vares to the north, at least for me, looks identical on all the three maps. And since the arrows are not there any more, which we have on the second map, it -- it looks better, at least as far as the map has been constructed here. But notwithstanding these comments, it -- it must be key for the corps commander to keep both shoulders of the Vares corridor open, to reinforce there in order to prevent the -- the forces of the Republika Srpska to cut from Vares north and from north to the south, to cut off his whole northern part of the defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So this must have been one of his key terrain and his key objectives, to keep this open at any rate -- at any cost.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one last question - and you referred to it, General, at the beginning - looking at -- given that this map has the complete territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, can you confirm that at this point in time, in July of 1993, the area of Central Bosnia was key not only to General Hadzihasanovic but was key to the survival of Bosnia and Herzegovina itself?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I just had the same expression before. This is the key terrain, the Central Bosnia, because all the main roads go through that. And if this key terrain is lost, the survival of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina doesn't make any -- it's very difficult. And it would bring the republic and even more pockets, because you still have the Bihac pocket in the north and the Gorazde pocket now and Srebrenica coming up pretty soon too. So this was a very difficult situation. And the mission for the 3rd Corps to keep this key terrain for the survival of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was a very difficult one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you very much, General, for highlighting these issues for us. Now, I would just like to confirm that from the documents you have read you did understand that both the HVO was an illegal armed force and that the VRS were also an illegal armed force.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this regard, the question of legitimacy and legal and non-legal is a thing which has to be discussed on a much higher level. But as far as I see what has happened by that time on those different courts, it was illegal from one side. But I think if you'd ask a Croat officer on the same question, he would see it differently. Therefore, I say I'm not quite sure -- I'm not that expert to call this illegal or non-legal forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Maybe my question was not precise enough, General. What I was referring to is which of the three armies, whether it was the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the army of the HVO, or the army of the VRS, which one of the armies is fighting a war defensively on its own territory against two aggressors?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, I wanted to highlight this situation, and now to come back on, despite this operational context, to go back to the documents we were looking at and the measures taken while fighting and while being occupied in this context. I would like you, General, to refer to binder number 1 that you were given yesterday concerning the measures.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I may ask you to turn to tab number 1. The theme for the others in the courtroom -- unfortunately do not have tabs. The theme is called, "Measures taken by ABiH 3rd Corps and its subordinate units in relation to training." General, we've had the opportunity yesterday to look at the title of each one of these documents; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we've had the opportunity to look a bit closer, because not in detail, due to lack of time, at the order of 10 July 1992 with respect to an order to form a training centre and to train recruits.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence would like to tender into evidence all the documents under tab 1, for the moment that they should be marked for identification as documents that the expert has identified as important documents in the light of the decisions taken by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, the Defence would like us to mark for identification all the documents under tab number 1, these documents being military orders, as we can see, with stamps, signatures, et cetera. What is the position of the Prosecution in that regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I -- if I could ask for some clarification. My learned colleague has referred to tendering them into evidence and also marking them for identification. I'm not sure if he wants them tendered into evidence, in which case they might be admitted, or if he simply wants them marked for identification. It's a bit unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You wish them to be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, for the moment, so as not to waste any time, but the Defence certainly does intend to produce these documents later on. We have already had lengthy debates with the Prosecution over these documents. I am not saying that they should be admitted now but for the present only marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution has noted the subtleness of the request of the Defence. They only wish the documents to be marked for identification, even though you have tendered almost identical documents which have been contested. So anyway, at this stage they're being marked for identification. What are your observations, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Two brief -- two brief observations, if I might. First, Mr. President, I'm not sure - and it doesn't need to be resolved at this point - I'm not sure about the lengthy debates about these documents that my learned colleague referred to. The Prosecution -- we're still evaluating the documents that were provided to us yesterday, but most of these documents the Prosecution has never seen before. But I leave that to another day. Mr. President, in order to save time, I'm not sure if my learned colleague is planning on marking all the documents for identification, but if his point is simply to have the documents marked for identification, the Prosecution has no objection with respect to all the documents provided yesterday in tabs 1 through 10 being marked for identification. Of course, the documents at tab 11 are already in evidence, so I don't mention those at the moment. But if they want to mark all the documents in all ten of the tabs, we have no objection to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, will you give us a number for all these documents under tab 1, which should be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH154 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, DH150D covers all the documents under tab 1. So we don't need DH150-1, -2, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is a global document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 12 documents together under a single number.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... tab 2 of the binder you have been provided with. And I refer to the documents in this tab as being judgements by the district military court in Zenica. And yesterday we went through some of the documents, General, under this tab, and namely, we did look at the first four documents.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you please tell -- give me the tab again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, tab number 2, General. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, I'm sorry. I thought binder number 2. Okay, I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tab number 2. Can you confirm, General, that we have together yesterday looked at the first four documents under this heading, and that was the request from the 3rd Corps Command for information, and then there were the Military Police Battalion. One was a monthly report; one was for a report over a longer period of time; and one was a report from the district military prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm, General, that these judgements are measures which can be attributed to General Hadzihasanovic, in terms of these referred to events or apparent violations committed by members of the 3rd Corps which have led to a final judgement?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to tender these documents and have them marked for identification. It's a series of documents which will be tendered in a bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, Defence is requesting that these documents be marked for identification, all the documents under tab 2. We have documents of two types: Either orders or reports between the 3rd Corps and the military court; and then we have judgements which were delivered against a number of individuals. These judgements, according to the Defence, are illustrated by the documents that are beneath the bundle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. President, in the event we weren't clear previously, the Prosecution has no objection to any of these materials being marked for identification, including all the documents in all of the first ten tabs of the material provided to us yesterday. We have no problem with any of those documents being marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, with regard to all the documents under tab 2 in binder 1, could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. President, the number for this bundle of documents will be DH155 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will move on to the next series of questions. The reason for which I'm dealing with these documents by series is that the comments of the expert witness will be important when determining the admissibility of these documents, and this is why I want to proceed on the basis of the subjects dealt with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... tab number 3 of the binder, under the theme, "Investigation and inspection."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you read, please, General, the title of the three documents that are in the first page, just the title, and the date, please.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first is 11/05/1993. It's, "Order, organisation and realisation of team tours, inspection of and assistance to units of the 3rd Corps and planning of team tours and inspection tours -- inspection of units, command, and troops of the 3rd Corps." And then there's another one, almost a month later, 08/06/93 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the witness please slow down when reading for the benefit of the interpreters, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sure. Excuse me, please, I apologise. The 8th of June, 1993, "A criminal report against unknown perpetrator, destruction of cultural and historical monuments and record on investigation." And the third -- that rings a bell, yeah. And the third is the 15th of June, 1993, "A report of the commission for establishing factual situation in the villages of Susanj and Ovnak."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, General. [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to have these documents marked for identification. These are three documents which will be filed as a bundle. Could we have a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, it appears that the second of these three documents already bears the number Defence -- or DH66, based on the markings at the top right of that document. Again, we have no objection, but it appears that one of these three documents is already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's quite right, Mr. President, but nevertheless I would like to file these documents as a bundle. And when discussing the admissibility of the documents, we could withdraw a document that already has a number. That would enable us to proceed more rapidly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have a number for the documents under tab 3. We have three documents, but it has been pointed out the second one already has a number, DH66, but could we have a number for the bundle.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number for the bundle of documents will be DH156 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... of the binder, under the heading "Protest letters." I would refer you to in the list of documents which is the first page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in order perhaps to save time here, the Prosecution is prepared to state for the record that we have no objection to any of the documents being admitted into evidence. If it's simply a question of them wanting this witness to identify what's in the bundles based on the titles, that may or may not be the best use of our limited time. With respect to all the documents in the first ten tabs of this material that was provided to us yesterday, the Prosecution has no objection to all of these documents going into evidence, if my learned colleague so wishes to do that, they can be marked and tendered and admitted into evidence, and we have no objection to all these documents being admitted into evidence. I simply raise that as a way perhaps to save some of our limited time. We're not going to be contesting these documents that were provided to us yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Bourgon, do continue. In fact, you wanted to ask the witness whether he was familiar with these documents, and if he had known about these documents would this have changed anything in his report. That was your purpose, was it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... I will -- from my colleague from the Prosecution, I will simply move on to quickly go through each of the tabs and have you read the theme; whereas, tab number 4 talks about protest letters, can you confirm that you have answered earlier to the fact that protest letters are indeed something that can be important, in terms of both prevention and suppression of violations of international humanitarian law?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen protest letters from both sides, and I think they are an important part, but I'm not familiar with those here under tab 4, as far as I see right now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: But basically I concur with your attitude -- or with your assumption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Can you please move to tab number 5, under the heading, "Legal measures."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But we need a number. Mr. Registrar, could we have a number for all the documents under tab 4.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number for this bundle will be DH157 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Tab number 5, "Legal measures." And all these documents come from either the legal sector of either the 3rd Corps or of one of the brigades. And you have confirmed that having a legal department and the endeavour to have a well-functioning legal department is also important in the business of prevention and suppression of violations.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to have a number for all the documents under tab number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've been requested to give a number to the bundle of documents under tab number 5, some documents of a legal nature that were signed by General Hadzihasanovic. We should also point out that there are documents bearing General Hadzihasanovic's signature and the signature is not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's quite right, Mr. President, and that is why we would just like to mark these documents for identification for the moment, in order to state our position with regard to these documents. So the Defence won't adopt a different position from the one adopted with regard to the documents tendered by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm talking about document 177O. Apparently the signature is not the General's signature. He usually signs in a legible manner. His signature is usually legible. In fact, his signature is his name, and it's easy to read. Having said that, could we have a number for all the documents under tab 5, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number for this bundle will be DH158 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous [Previous translation continues] ... tab 6, under the heading, "Joint command," and ask you to confirm that the establishment of a joint command, especially in the situation in which General Hadzihasanovic operated, namely, having a former ally who has become his enemy, the endeavour to form a joint command to work together again are indeed important measures.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we have a number for the documents. There are seven documents in a bundle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have a number for the bundle of seven documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number for this bundle of documents will be DH159 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... tab number 7, under the heading, "Other measures taken by ABiH 3rd Corps and its subordinate units." And I would like you to refer to the third document on the first page, to say -- to look at the type of documents. And this one is a request to send an inspection to the Secretariat of National Defence, and this document was sent to the District Secretariat of Defence in Travnik. The -- I would like also to refer you to the document -- the last one -- the before-last document, the document dated 13 September 1993. And this document is entitled "Order, a ban on entering public establishments." Are these types of measures and orders that can be effective for the prevention and the topping of violations -- stopping of violations of either discipline, criminal acts, or violations of international humanitarian law?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I would like to be helpful. But as long as I don't know what the contents is -- just to send an inspection team some place doesn't mean anything to me in this regard. If I see on order imbalance of units, it doesn't tell me something about morale and discipline, and law and order. So it might be that you're right, but I cannot really assure that this is the way it's written down in those documents because I just don't know them, sir. And I had no time to scan or to even read them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I fully appreciate, General. And I really also wish to express my appreciation for your help in these circumstances, being shown that many documents. Maybe we can actually go to the before-last document, dated 13th of September.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is a document -- so maybe, General, to go more quickly, if I look at the document dated the 3rd of October.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one is it? I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. The dates -- there seems to be a date problem.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you refer to the first document, General, the one dated the 7th of March. And can you look at this document. I was hoping to get a shorter document, and that's why I was referring to the last one. Can you please have a glance at this document, which is addressed to commands of all brigades, to Municipal Defence Staff, and headquarters support units. And this document deals with the joint application of security measures and to create a joint commission that will define the competencies, tasks, and duties of this commission. And it goes on to talk about the composition of the commission.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And lists the duties of the commission, including such things as duration and control of curfew.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That looks very sensible to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we look at the second page of this document, we look at paragraph number 3, where it talks about the formation of special purpose MUP units - MUP being, as you know from the documents you have read, the civilian police component.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Such measures, if the other documents under this heading are similar documents and similar measures, can you confirm that all measures taken by the 3rd Corps headquarters to regulate the way the army conducts its business and the way the soldiers will behave are important for the prevention of violations?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we have a number for the documents under tab 7. There are eight documents under this tab, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have a number for these eight documents.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number for this bundle of documents will be DH160 ID.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to go to binder number 2, General, please.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Under tab number 8, we have a theme called, "Preventive measures in relation to alleged incidents." I would like you to turn to the second document, the one dated 18 April 1993.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document, General - I have the document before me - and can you confirm that this is dated 18 April 1993, this is to all units in Zenica, and the document is, at least under the signature block of the chief of security for the 3rd Corps, and that this talks about urgently taking all necessary measures to prevent plunder of facilities in town and regions of combat activities. Can you confirm that such orders and such measures being issued by the chief of security would be measures that are very important to prevent and also to suppress and repress violations?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this particular case, General, I would like you to refer to the date 18th of April, 1993. Does this date remind you of a specific incident in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I remember, that this was shortly before -- before the things happened in Miletici, but I don't know exactly what on the 18th of April happened, or maybe the 17th of April happened. Because it must refer to something which happened before the 18th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I suggest to you, General, that on the 16th of April, 1993 was probably the -- the most -- the biggest massacre committed by the HVO in the town of Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this attack that was conducted by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read about this, but I'm not familiar, because this was not the case I was looking into.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, could you confirm that if there was such -- such an attack - and actually, before this Chamber this is a fact that has been admitted, that there was this attack on the 16th of April - but on the basis of our discussions yesterday, that this attack could have had an impact on the soldiers of the 3rd Corps and especially might have been very difficult on them if their close relatives or people from their own ethnic background lived in Ahmici. Would that be fair to say?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been difficult for them. I admit this, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And an order such as this one at this point in time would be very important in order to keep the soldiers under control and ensure that even though someone is from a Croat background, that we would protect their property and ensure that the soldiers would not commit violations.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we have a number for the documents under tab 8. It's a series of documents. The bundle consists of a total of 19 documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have a number for all the documents under tab 8.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number for this bundle of documents will be DH162 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have another five minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I go on quickly to the "Measures to protect" under tab 9, and I refer you simply to the title of the second document, which would be, "An order to the Operational Group Lasva to organise and take measures to connect forces of manoeuvre and area structure and the MUP with a view to protecting residents and property." Is that the type of order which can be very significant in preventing and suppressing violations?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we have a number for the documents under tab number 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, the previous number was DH162 ID; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President. The previous number should have been DH161 ID, and the new number should be DH162 ID. I apologise again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the three documents, "Measures for protection," DH162 ID will be the number for these documents. Mr. Bourgon, you have another four minutes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... last category of documents, because given that those under tab 11 are already evidence, these documents deal with fulfilling of obligations in respect to prisoners of war and exchange. Would you say, General, that it is very important for the parties to fulfil their obligations under the law with respect to the exchange of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, definitely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that it would be another very significant sign for the commanding general to cooperate and even to create a commission for the exchange of prisoners and to ensure that the agreements arising from such commissions are applied in good faith?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we have a number for the documents that have to do with respecting obligations when exchanging prisoners of war. These are documents under tab number 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we have a number for the 15 documents under tab 10.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The number will be DH163 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll go on to tab number 11. These have already been tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... cross-examination this morning by going back on the issue of measures as being one of the focuses of your expert report?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we moved on to looking at the maps and looking at the operational context to confirm that in this specific case the circumstances under which General Hadzihasanovic was operating were not -- not complex but probably the most complex circumstances that a military commander can be placed in.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, there's no question about it, and I think I also made it very clear in my statement how difficult the situation for the corps commander was to build up his corps, to fight the corps under very adverse conditions, and I think I -- I don't -- I don't envy him for the things he had to do in that time, because as from my professional point of view, it couldn't have been worse for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, this is a sensitive question, but we have just went through a series of documents which were not provided to you at the time of making -- of preparing your expert report. May I ask you how you feel about having been asked to prepare an expert report on measures without having been provided with such documents.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I don't really want to comment on that, because I have been issued additional material again and again and again. And on the one hand, I'm happy that I haven't had another 23 binders; on the other hand, the more material you get, the better it is to -- to base your statement on -- on facts and figures drawn from the documents. So I -- I don't know when the documents came up, and therefore I am -- it's very difficult for me to -- to judge here. I only tell you the better you are prepared, as far as the documents are concerned, to come up with an expert statement, the better it is for you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. Can you say, just before we move to the break, to what extent this changes your view on the situation and the exercise of command by General Hadzihasanovic in 1993 in the circumstances in which he was placed and the measures which were taken by him and his subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have stated in my statement, I found only one case until now. Now in those binders I found many other cases, and therefore I would revise my opinion that this was a singulary [sic] action. I would say that having seen all this material it shows that he has taken much more of his responsibility in an appropriate way than I thought before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you confirm that it is even surprising that an army could do all these measures in this context.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because I think this is a part of the mission, and there was a very clear legal mission also to the commanding general of the 3rd Corps. And what you have shown me now, it shows that he did his job according to the legal mission. But we discussed it also yesterday, notwithstanding the adverse operational problems, you just cannot put aside the legal question. So it's not astonishing, no. This is the way it should have been done, and I think General Hadzihasanovic has done as far as the problems are concerned where we just discussed the best way possible under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we can have the break now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have our break now, and we will resume at five to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
