utterances.text: [In English] General, we are closing in to the end of my cross-examination on behalf of the accused General Hadzihasanovic. I would like to address two issues at this time, and I would like to begin with the issue of the events which took place in Dusina in the month of January of 1993. From the documents that you were given, I take it that you are familiar with these events.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, in your report, when you referred to Dusina, am I right in saying that you did not provide very much -- or the details of the operation itself?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not asked to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And one of the questions you were asked to do is whether the general was aware of the -- what had happened in Dusina.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whether measures had been taken.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To move quickly with this issue, I would like you to -- to refer you to the map that is behind you, and I would like to point to a few areas on this map and ask you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should like to approach the map. Thank you. Mr. President, this is a map that I showed at the beginning of my cross-examination. It is a composition of several smaller maps, mostly being Defence exhibits. Others are new. And the totality now is one exhibit or one document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] [Previous translation continues] ... let me -- are you able to tell by looking at this map that this is a 1 to 25.000 map?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say so, yeah. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, on this particular map, there are two things that I would like to point out to you: First of all, the headquarters of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And there's -- there was a -- in the red is indicated - and these are the markings that were made by the Defence on a map that was empty, but I just want to ask you whether the markings in red here identify to you the orders that were issued to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. For the benefit of the records of these proceedings, I'm wondering if my learned colleague can tell us whether these markings are based on a hypothetical situation or if they are based on materials that in evidence before this Trial Chamber, and what the source, whether it's a trial transcript record or an exhibit, what is the source for the markings which the Defence have made. Or in the alternative, if we're dealing in the realm of hypothetical situations, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the markings in red on the map come from a document which was submitted by the Defence. It has been marked for identification. It has still not been admitted into evidence, but it refers to an order that was given by the Brigade Commander Jure Francetic, that is, General Totic, who testified in this chamber. And the information comes from a sketch that he himself made before the Chamber and which is being reproduced here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [In English] General, I would like you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are the explanations provided satisfactory for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't sitting here recall a sketch drawn by Mr. Totic. Perhaps if we could have the number. My learned friend says it was marked for identification. If we could have the number of that document, that might assist us in retrieving the document from our files.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall look for the document, Mr. President. Mr. President, the document is DH46 ID and DH44. I left the original in the office because I used it to make the markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I see. It's DH44. Mr. Registrar is going to give it to us. The Chamber will look at the document. So the red markings were made by you on the basis of indications given by General Totic; is that right? The indications to be found on document DH44.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, together with the arrows.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue. We're following.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To make things quicker, I would simply ask you one question. And ignore the markings in red. I would simply ask you to take a look, please, at the Lasva junction, which you are familiar with on the basis of the documents that you have read, and to please confirm -- if you can please look at the Lasva junction. To make it easier, I will point this junction to you. And on the basis of this map on the 1 to 25.000, could you please elaborate on the importance of this specific junction for the commanding general of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Well, it's -- it's important because two -- excuse me, it's important because two major roads are joining there; one along the Lasva Valley, which I think was a major road, and the other one going to Kaonik and from there into the western side for the area of operations. So the Lasva junction for him was important to keep it open for two major roads of supply and, I would also say, of communications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Would you agree with me, General, that by losing this junction, the Lasva Valley junction, that this would simply cut off the main road which was linking Zenica, here, to Travnik and Vitez, here?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think this is what I just explained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you on this map -- do you recall from the documents that you have been -- that you have consulted whether there were events in the same time frame as Dusina which took place in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I concentrated on Dusina, as this was the key issue, and this was also one of the first encounters between the HVO and the Bosnian forces. I did not -- I did not look into the other case you just mentioned. I'm not familiar with that one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. I would ask you, with the permission of the Trial Chamber, if you could come and take a look at the model. And I would like you to comment from a military perspective and an operational perspective the location of the Lasva Valley junction and where -- whether to have -- and I would ask you to come this way, please, General. I will indicate to the Lasva Valley junction. Whereas Zenica is here. And can you point with -- towards the Lasva Valley junction.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Yes. Could you please leave the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you use the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... and have a close-up, please. Now, General, just above the Lasva Valley junction, there is a hill indicated with -- over here. Can you confirm that from a military and a tactical perspective this was probably the best area to control this junction.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's one of the possibilities. I don't know whether it's the best one because --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness use a microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I think the scale of that map here is so large that it's very difficult. And now we're really talking small tactics, very small tactics, company level and below. This hill is always very important to overwatch a road junction, but I don't know whether this was the proper one, this one, or whether he would have done it down in the valley. I don't know. I think this is not to be seen from that kind of sketch here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General, I would like to -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the documents you have been given, what you can say about the events in January, in terms of what exactly was the event which took place on the 26th of January, 1993, if you know.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I also referred to the material issued to me yesterday from you, because even so this is called a hypothetical case, I think it's not hypothetical at all. I don't know why we have this term. But at least this was an encounter between -- a military clash between the HVO and the ABiH I think for the very first time, and it's obvious that the commanding general of the 3rd Corps tried everything to prevent it. On the other hand, he knew that if something happens there, he had to fight for that. And there was a clash. This was not a big battle. It was small, a very small battle, where both sides had some very minor casualties. I say that because I think we have to see about the size of the operations going on by that time. And in the battle, some HVO soldiers surrendered and I think which made that case infamous or famous, why we're talking about this right now, is that five of those -- or four of those surrendered -- soldiers surrendered from the HVO have been killed afterwards. So it's a small happening, but for the outbreak of the violations between the Bosnian and the Croat forces I think it was very important, and that's probably also the reason why ECMM intervened immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. Now, I -- it was difficult to try to highlight the material that was given to you and the material that was not given to you in respect of Dusina. We tried to isolate this material. What I would like to do -- to do at this time is to highlight for you some of the principal characteristics of what happened during that period and then ask you to comment. This is based on the information which was provided to you yesterday, so we may call it hypothetical because this was the -- what the Defence was trying to do to save some time and to not show you every single document. Correct me if I am right, General, did you understand from the material given to you that there was a build-up on the part of the HVO leading to the actions taken by General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that General Hadzihasanovic on the basis of the material provided to you - and I'm talking the Defence material - that he issued orders in the way it would be expected of a commanding general, even though this was a very small operation, but due to the importance of the Lasva Valley junction he issued his orders to place his troops while asking of them restraint? Could you confirm that on the basis of the material given to you?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, this is true. And he even did a restriction which was very strange for me, that the final goal for the fighting of his forces would be dependent on his agreement. So it was the corps commander himself who basically looked into the battle in -- in all its little aspects in order to prevent an outbreak too early by leaving it to lower-level command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And from this material, can you confirm that not only did he keep the last order to proceed with the use of force to himself but that he also warned his forces and his subordinate units that they were to at any possibility avoid a conflict with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. He didn't want to be called the one who had started the operation. He wanted to make absolutely sure this was the other side which started the hostilities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, we discussed -- the material provided to you indicates that following that two -- sorry. To conduct this operation, the General deployed the Zenica Municipal Defence Staff. Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That he deployed with that a company of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that later on, just before, on the 25th, he also deployed a reinforced company from the 303 Brigade to go towards the line between Merdani and Dusina.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that's a part of the papers -- of the orders I have been given to you. It's -- yeah, that's the -- it's number 20. Right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if the material given to you was true in the sense that on the 25th of January the HVO broke the line and that they were getting closer to this junction and to Dusina and that General Hadzihasanovic reported to the Supreme Command this situation but also that he was going to take the necessary measures to reinforce the Lasva Valley junction, would that be a proper thing to do for a commanding general?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for a commanding general to deploy his mortars on -- in Janjici, about five kilometres away or a little less from this junction in support of operations in the Lasva Valley junction, would that also be the proper thing to do?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether this is the proper thing to do for a commanding general of a corps. I come back to what I said before, because the commander really now coordinated a very, very small-scale tactical-level operations. But maybe since this was the first operation breaking out he just wanted to make sure that nothing happens which was not in consonance with his ideas. But this would normally not be the normal way for a commanding general, to move a company and to talk about the employment of the company. This is down to, at the most, at the best a battalion commander and not the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, in the material provided to you, it is indicated that there was some kind of a clash on the 26th of January and that a series of reports were then produced --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- following this event.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I list the reports that were highlighted in the material given to you, which begins with a report from the 1st Company of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade talking about five HVO soldiers captured at 10.00 and that this specific subunit had returned to barracks.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A further report by the Municipal Defence Staff -- now, the Municipal Defence Staff were the lead unit, can you confirm this on the basis of this information?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they provided a report to the district staff, which is kind of the headquarters of the TO, to which they were still reporting at the time, that they reported that three HVO had been killed, that three had been wounded, and five or six captured.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next report was by the district staff on the basis of the former report reported in the interim to the 3rd Corps that there had been fighting and that they had -- they reported the same information they had received from the Municipal Defence Staff. This was followed by a report by 7 Brigade directly to the 3rd Corps operations centre talking about five HVO who had been killed and -- made prisoners and 25 HVO who had been made prisoner in Lasva. There were two further reports according to this scenario; one at 6.00 by the district staff confirming their event on the 26th of January, and then the 3rd Corps reporting this information to the Supreme Command the night of the 26th of January. General, on the basis of this information, if that information is true, would that be the normal way for information to be reported from the subunit all the way up to the 3rd Corps and to army command?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say so. And it also shows that the problem of communications which we discussed before was not existent here. So all levels were in close communication and very fast communication because these were on-spot reports, as we would call them, and it was -- they were capable in the time of highest tension to get all this information through to highest headquarters. So notwithstanding the -- the technicalities, at least the communication worked pretty well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, here from a military perspective there is something that attracted my attention, and that's what I would like to ask you: It appears that the 1st Company of the 2nd Battalion of the 7th Brigade made two reports; one to the Municipal Defence Staff and one to the 3rd Corps. Would that be a proper procedure, to have two reports from the same company in this particular scenario?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think this was a very unusual situation. It was the first outbreak. They were under the command of the Municipal Staff, so they reported to them. At the same time, the -- the brigade was still under the direct command of the 3rd Corps, so they also informed the 3rd Corps, because they had two ways of command and control, being that detached company under the Municipal Staff. So I think it might be a little bit irregular, but as I know, in times of tension you -- you used to give more information and to give -- to have a much denser message flow than you would normally have. This was not the routine by -- for the forces by that particular time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, we -- based on this information, unless -- because we discussed this issue before. Unless the commanding general receives any specific information to the contrary, was it reasonable for him to believe that operations had been conducted in the way they should have been?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we move on under the same scenario, General, there was a report which was addressed by the commanding general to the supreme headquarters where they reported that the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps, who had attended a meeting on the 27th of January, said that the commander of the HVO, Colonel Blaskic, did not want to participate in this meeting any more because of allegations of seven people killed in Lasva. This information, according to this, if it is true, was immediately reported to Supreme Command headquarters. Would that be the proper way to do things for a commanding general who hears about this allegation?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And further to this report, we see that the next day, on the 28th, there was another -- further information which was provided again from the commanding general to the Supreme Command and with a detailed timetable of all the events in Dusina. Would that also be reasonable for the commanding general, having heard of allegations, reporting them to his superior headquarters, and then checking the information and reporting back and saying that this has been a normal engagement?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the -- the one you're talking about right now is on the 28th; right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the 28th.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would not be normal to air this on Croatian radio. If you go to your higher headquarters, this is a very -- a very strange way to connect -- to communicate with higher headquarters, through Croatian radio. But the content of what you're saying I think is appropriate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, maybe the example that was given to you was not particularly clear, but on the 28th there were -- or 27th or 28th there were allegations made on Croatian radio that there had been killings.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what -- having heard the information on the radio, having heard about the allegations made by Colonel Blaskic, on one hand, but on the other hand, having all these reports internal and having checked the information, would it be reasonable for the commander to weigh the information and to report his conclusions to his superior headquarters?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we see from this scenario that further on there was an identification of the bodies that were picked up on the battlefield and that this was done by the Zenica Security Service and the Ministry of the Interior. And I also note there that there was an official test conducted; they call it a paraffin test. This information was not provided to you, but this is a hypothetical: I simply say for the record that the paraffin test is simply to say if people had gunpowder on their hands and whether they had been firing weapons at that time.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the results of that test were then, along with the identity of the people who died, provided to the district military court in Zenica. If General Hadzihasanovic, if these events are true -- if General Hadzihasanovic had the belief on the basis of the internal reports provided to him through his subordinate chain of command that there had been no offence and these events had taken place by the organisation which was responsible to pick up the bodies, who did identify the body, who did do a test, and who did report it to the district military court, whether there was an offence or not committed, did the general accomplish his duty of ensuring that these events will be followed up upon?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he believed that what he has been told by lower headquarters, that they were not included in these alleged crimes, if he believes in that, then -- then you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you expect, General, that the commanding general would proceed himself to Dusina to check?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I add to this scenario the fact that any witnesses to the killing, if there were any, were not available, would that help you to -- would that assist the commanding general in believing the information he was provided with?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: If people are being killed, you normally have witnesses. I would at least have sent my own organs, like military police, security forces, to check into that, because I think this was the first real thing in -- in the war, the first outbreak. Therefore, it was not the normality. Normally the size of operations, I think, was a very small one. But since this had such a big bearing for the rest of the operations, as far as a component of the forces was concerned, I would have done at least my own -- not my own personal, but I would have sent my organs available for that to check into that and make absolutely sure that nothing has happened which could be brought on the shoulders of my soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, given all the information that you have in this specific scenario, would you conclude that there was any attempt whatsoever on the commanding general to hide information?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't have this intention -- this -- I don't think this is what he has done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Impression. I did not have this impression.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if the documents and the evidence shows that what was possibly -- what could be done possibly in the circumstances, given, of course, the circumstances even with which we have described, where there is still fighting going on in many areas, would it be normal for the general to, having been -- having convinced himself that there were no offences, to move on to other issues and to continue waging his war and fulfilling all of his other responsibilities which he had to do at the same time?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, it seems that the general was not very happy with the situation of his own forces; otherwise, he wouldn't have given an order almost after this happening where he talks about occurrences of looting and plundering and disbehaviour of his own soldiers and tells them that they should adhere to the provisions of the international law. So it seems that there has -- happened some things he was not very happy with but he thought by that time, by -- at least, this is my interpretation, that by giving these orders - and he gave two in a very short period of time, on the 1st and 3rd of February; at least, these re the ones in my hand - where he shows his discontent with the behaviour of the troops on the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, of course, these orders, General, you've seen these orders, and these orders don't mention the issue of killing but they mention the issue of plunder.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've noticed, General, by looking at the indictment -- or maybe you don't know. But if I tell you that any allegations of plundering in Dusina have been withdrawn, would you establish, then, a link between these orders and the situation in Dusina or maybe with another situation because he has a whole area to look after?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it was another situation because the word "Dusina" doesn't appear in -- in either of the two documents I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, one last thing on Dusina before moving on quickly to the last issue, and that is dealing -- because in your report you refer to a meeting which took place on 1 February, and you mention in your report that this meeting was initiated by the HVO and that there must have been the issue was placed on the agenda and that it must have been known also by General Morillon. I don't have time, General, to show you and run you through the documents, but if I tell you, General, that this meeting was basically the meeting at which the joint command was created and that this was the meeting which was actually initiated by General Hadzihasanovic - and we didn't have time to go through the protest letters, but in the protest letter he suggested these talks - how would you interpret the actions of General Hadzihasanovic in such a scenario?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe I might quote -- maybe I don't understand English enough, but it says in the paper signed by General Hadzihasanovic on 1st February: "On the request of the HVO Croatian Defence Council," so it doesn't say, "On my request" -- "through the mediations of General Morillon and with the approval of Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command a joint meeting was held." So I just refer to what I found in my papers here. And I think that Morillon went there on behalf somehow to mediate between the two warring factions by that time. And it doesn't say very much in detail, just says what the outcome was. At the end, again General Hadzihasanovic tells his brigade commander, "Prohibit all members of the army from stealing, looting, burning property, arrest perpetrators, and so on." So he took, as I said, his first impressions about the first happenings in the war and portrayed his impressions to his brigade commanders, telling them, "I'm not very happy what has happened there." And two days later he even went further to -- to sign a special order to all his brigade commanders where he said, "We'd like to stick with the humanitarian approach of the international law and make sure that your soldiers do this as well." So he has taken his consequences of what he was informed of, either by his commander or by the ECMM in this regard, or by General Morillon - I don't know who in person informed him on that - but again, I don't know how much he basically looked after the -- the killing or the alleged killing of those five HVO soldiers who have surrendered, and I think this -- and I come back to that. I think this would have been a very important thing, because once you kill soldiers of the other side who have surrendered, you start up a spiral of violence against your own soldiers which is very detrimental, and therefore I think it's very important to look into that particular case in order to prevent things like this happening again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what the -- if I tell you, General, that the -- the actual meeting of the 1 February -- and again, I don't have sufficient time, maybe we can come back to that. But that this meeting was not related to the event in Dusina but that there were meetings earlier on with the commander of BritBat in which this was discussed. Now, I ask you that when you look at all these events, in terms of the way -- the preparation or the build-up towards this attack, the way the attack was conducted by the HVO, the way the ABiH responded by defending the territory, and then all the reports issued by -- or received by General Hadzihasanovic and the way he reported it to the superior headquarters, went out to check and get more information, reported the -- the detailed chronology to his supreme headquarters, and then the issue was handled [sic] over to the district military court. Do you find any, in these course of events, if that was the case, do you find any way to say that General Hadzihasanovic was not a -- did not act as a reasonable commander in the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. If this is the way you just portrayed it, which I cannot find in the documents, and you said he sent somebody to look into the matter - I don't know that - I only can base my assumptions on the documents issued to me. If this is the case, as you just portrayed it, that's different from the impression I had. And then I agree with your -- with your assumption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But even on the documents that you've received and the fact that he did report the matter twice to supreme headquarters, you didn't -- you cannot know there's any -- any possibility or any inference that he was trying to hide something or that he was trying to -- to do away with the situation.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I never said this, and I would never implicate that. That's not the case, not at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. I'd like to move on to the last issue in my cross-examination and this is also an issue in your report and that deals with an issue of the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I confirm, General, that when you took on this assignment to become the -- an expert witness on behalf of the Prosecution, that you had no specific knowledge on -- on the issue of Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I had the same knowledge as every European reader of the papers, that there were Mujahedin, that they have committed atrocities, and that there are probably still some Mujahedin in the country right now. I know from my discussion which I had once with the president of Bosnia and Herzegovina how important for him the support of the Arab countries was; morally and even more so financially. But I -- I was not informed about details as I have seen them now in those papers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in terms of the links between the religious community in Bosnia and the Mujahedin, you have no information to that effect?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. Not so whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or in terms of the source of financing or the source of getting weapons of these Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't had any information on this before, rather than the Mujahedin have been in the country and took part in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And am I right in saying that on the basis of your report you, of course, mentioned that the material which was provided to you, you mentioned the word it was rather limited in order to form a clear view as to what really happened with those Mujahedin in 1993.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sir, it's still -- it's still somehow blurred for me. Because on the one hand, they were called soldiers, and there is evidence that they were called soldiers by the commanders of the Bosnian forces. And they themselves said, "We joined to some extent the territorial organisation right at the beginning and worked with them." They were being taken care of in a rather detailed way by the 7th Mountain Brigade for looking for lost persons, and they said, "These are soldiers which we are looking for." They were working within the battalions or cooperating within the battalions. On the other hand, I don't know whether is a part of a real organisational structure under which they worked. But one thing for me is clear: Based on the material given to me that the Mujahedin were operating on the battlefield and in some ways very closely with the forces on the ground, spearheading them, and supporting them, and also creating problems for them, and that it then took a lot of -- a lot of work for the -- for the brass of the Bosnian army to incorporate them into the Bosnian army as an entity, and even so at the end of the year they were not officially under control because people were still concerned about what they -- what they did and how they did it. And this is a clear deduction just from the sources, the documents given to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, the -- you mentioned "they," they the Mujahedin. You talk about "they," and you've referred to that earlier on. But I take it that you refer to the issue because in response to questions by my colleague you referred to a video. Am I right in saying that this video was your main source of information on the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not right. You're not right. I have a whole list of documents here which are documents from the 3rd Corps, from the 7th Mountain Brigade, from the 306th Brigade, under which heading they were -- amongst whom they were working. So it's not only this one video. I only took this video to show how the Mujahedin themselves saw them and the evolution when they came in country in the summer of 1999 and how from their point of view they tried to hook up with the institutions and organisations working in the country, and I don't know about the purpose of this video, but I thought the way this has been portrayed, it shows, at least not only a one side but also the other side concerning what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, this video, you don't know who produced the video. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. You were not informed, at least, as to who produced the video.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it -- it always talks about the Shura, the war council of the Mujahedin, which were interested to -- to demonstrate what they have done in that time and also somehow to -- to -- how should I say? To memorise the martyrs; i.e., those Mujahedin which have been killed during those battles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the -- you mentioned in your examination-in-chief that you had not seen the video; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only have the transcript of the text which is underlining the video which I have never seen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you don't know who wrote this text.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this -- when I look at the -- you are -- you will agree with me that if we want to determine the true relationship that could have existed or the true motif of the Mujahedin, it would be important to have -- to know and to speak to the Mujahedins themselves.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't have any document by the Mujahedin, but I thought rather than having it only from one side, i.e., the documents -- the orders by the Bosnian army, this is a supplement, which doesn't bring anything new. It just is a supporting factor of what I had drawn out from the other documents. And I have no reason to believe that this is all wrong, what they -- how they portrayed it themselves. And I think it's -- it's the way a very good help because it coincides in some ways very much to what General Hadzihasanovic writes in his reports about the time, about the -- the way of -- of the cooperation which had happened at the very early time. So I think it's rather obvious that if this is a source which I don't feel like being a wrong propaganda, I don't have the -- any reason not to believe that this is true. I have not any reason that this has been alleged afterwards. I think it's a self-portrait of the Mujahedin which I think it's worthwhile to look into.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I would provide you, General, with another book on the Mujahedin by another expert on Mujahedin which provides you with different information, you could also be tempted to use the book and say, "It's very interested because it can help me in knowing what happened in Bosnia."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. Being a historian, I know how difficult it is to qualify the sources from which you draw your information. You have to analyse them and you have to look from them. And, therefore, I contradicted when you told me that I based all my information on that video, because this is just not true. I had most of the time worked without the video. I got the video at one of the very last encounters, where I got the video and the Blaskic statements of the two -- the two gentlemen, which was withdrawn then. But before that, for me, based on the documents given to me, the documents prepared or produced by the 7th Mountain Brigade, by the 306th Brigade, and by the 3rd Corps headquarters, for me it was very obvious that there was some kind of close cooperation in the preparation and the conduct of operations. And if you are responsible for an operation, the -- the forces fighting with you, working with you, whether they're official under your supervision or not, you become responsible for what happened in the operation which you planned and executed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that is -- that is if they take part in your operation and that is if they take part with you?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you could not identify this in terms of the documents and the material that was given to you.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at least the -- the 306th Brigade was very clear that they -- they -- at least, the brigade commander, I must say, not the brigade, that he was very much against the conduct of the operation in Miletici, where -- where civilians were killed afterwards. And it also shows, at least in -- in two cases, where after a battle has been taken care of a responsible representative of the 7th Mountain Brigade went into the area where the forces were still available, trying to find out what happened, and looting happened, and the looting could not be -- could not be prevented any more and the discipline could not be reinstated because forces which participated in that -- in that operation before were opposing law and order, were even opposing the attempt of the military police to restate law and order. So if that happened, I would assume that the same forces which were there doing their part in the looting business also participated in -- in the operation before. And I also have indications, as I stated in my paper, that at least the Mujahedin proposed clear training for BiH forces -- Bosnian forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have reference to this?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I have reference to this. They said, "We offered -- we offered the best guys from that battalion to come with us." And I think even general --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Hadzihasanovic in his paper to higher headquarters basically lays down that there were Turks and Arabs training soldiers for the guerilla type of warfare. So --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not my words.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The information you're referring to now about the training also comes from that video; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said one comes from the video. But also, in -- in that demand for establishing or asking higher headquarters what to do about the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you, General, a few documents just to go over and to finish my cross-examination. And this is a series of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I would like to issue to distribute this documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to confirm with you a few issues before closing my cross-examination at 12.00, as promised.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: But, sir, you just cut me off when I was just trying to finish a sentence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I think I should --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please go ahead, General. I don't want to cut you off.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I should be in a possibility, because I think this is important also for the Court. That this is not only based on the video. It says - and this is a paper signed by General Hadzihasanovic on 13 June - that: "There have been volunteers from foreign countries as well as a group of Bosnians trained by them, the so-called guerilla." So they have -- this is not a video. This is General Hadzihasanovic saying that the guerilla have been trained by them. And in the order of the 13th of August, it says: "Replenish the El Mujahed detachment with foreign volunteers --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down when reading, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "These people keep the weapons and other equipment which have been issued to them." So it's probably the Bosnian army who issued them the weapons. I just want to make sure that we don't have a one-side look at this particular case. That doesn't mean that they were incorporated all the time in the army, but it shows that even on the side of General Hadzihasanovic there was some kind of cooperation with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we have a look at these documents, General, because this is exactly the same documents you were looking at. And I would simply like you to confirm some of the informations that is found in these documents. And the first document -- and I would like to go one by one very quickly, because unfortunately I'm running out of time -- and the general here mentions in his letter to the supreme headquarters - he is writing to Commander Delic and to the Chief of Staff, Halilovic - and can you confirm that what he says in there in the first line is that since the beginning there have been volunteers from foreign countries?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He says that. And he says that there's a group of Bosnians -- and he's not talking about soldiers who have been trained by them. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm that these guerillas he's referring to is the mix of the Mujahedin and the Bosnians who have not entered the ranks of the army?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you confirm that they had been invited to and they refused to do so, according to this letter?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have been invited and they have refused to. And we also know, sir, that in those battalions of the 7th Mountain Brigade there were organisations, the guerilla organisations, which were organic parts of the brigades.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I go on, General, with -- when it says that: "These people are still contemplating proposals made to them by the Army Chief of Staff."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would indicate that there is something going on --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- between the army and between this guerilla group, who is not in the army. And then it says: "They don't want to make public their decisions regarding whether or not they will join the army," which means that they haven't joined the army at this time. And: "They only want to talk to top officials and not the 3rd Corps commander."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that they don't want to talk to them.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's obvious that they didn't want to talk to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that in the opinion of these people, according to General Hadzihasanovic, all that is wanted is that they want him to fix a meeting with the top brass.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he confirms in the next paragraph that: "These people were in the territory even before the 3rd Corps was created."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he says, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that they've been fighting using unlawful or at least methods that are outside lawful methods of combat, and this is the problems you were referring to. These people were fighting and what they were doing was detrimental to the state of BH. Is that what the general is saying?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's what he says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is the general also saying that these Muslims also have a link with clergymen and who are behind them? Is that what the general is saying in this letter?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about the next paragraph, General, where the general says: "Negotiations have started and finding a solution with the highest level of the RBH." Isn't that the general confirming that there are something going on, there is something going on with the army and these people but that is completely foreign to him?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he doesn't know exactly what's going on, but there is something going on. There's no question about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's something going on. But he doesn't know what's going on. You would agree with me, according to this letter.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what he says is that he does not want to be held accountable --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- for the consequences of these people's actions, which is a bit different from what you mentioned in answer to the Prosecution when you responded that he no longer wants to be held accountable. Is there a difference between he does not want to be held accountable or no longer held accountable? You would agree with me that there is a difference between the two?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he, I think, he is not accountable. He doesn't feel accountable for what has happened with the Mujahedin in his area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we move -- thank you, General. Can we move to the second document. And this is the -- a follow-up to General Hadzihasanovic's letter. And if you look at the date of 16th June, so it is immediately following. Would you confirm, General, that the first paragraph of this letter is a direct reference to General Hadzihasanovic's letter?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that this letter, the last line of this beginning: "The order is the aim of their focus, engagement, and our struggle." Now, these are not the words of General Hadzihasanovic. These are added by supreme headquarters, who for the first time say in writing that they have an aim of focussing their engagement into the Bosnian struggle. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the order is twofold: The order is to send them to Igman and to merge them with the independent detachment in Zuka's unit." Can you confirm, General that, the SDK independent detachment in Zuka's unit is, based on the information you've been provided, an independent unit attached and subordinated directly to the army and not a unit in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the unit of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the second part of the order, of course, is he says: "If they don't accept this, if they don't want to go to Mount Igman, then you show them no hospitality and eventually, if you have to, disarm them." Is this what this order is saying?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the commander, of course, is requesting information as to the measures to implement this order. Now, I'd like to show you the next document. And I'm not sure if you have received this document or not. You do -- have received this document. And this is a phone conversation between General Halilovic and with General Hadzihasanovic. At least, this is what you used this order for in your report. Now, the Defence position on this document, General, is that it is a telephone conversation, and we have not admitted this document because we have some doubt as to the source. But if this document is true, then we look at the second page, and there is a question that comes from -- the information is the following: And it says, line 15 of page 2.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where it says: "Regarding the information that we have received about those foreigners." Now, you agree that this is a person's name with a Delta that speaking.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And General Halilovic then says, "Yes. And Hadzihasanovic answers: "It cannot be done that way." Is that what the general is saying?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he's saying, "If I do this, this is going to be my third front line." And he says, "No, no, it's ordered here. The two of them have signed it." Who are -- do you know who the "two of them," he is referring to, who Halilovic is referring to as "the two of them"?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think it's -- it's the representative of the Mujahedin, on the one side, and the representative which has been sent to them, on the other side, by Delic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, he's talking -- isn't he talking in this paragraph about the letter that -- about the order itself? Isn't he talking about the order? "It is ordered here. Two of them have signed it."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it might also be the order. I don't know. I only know that there was a special representative sent there because they were not very cooperative at the beginning, and maybe this was a letter which has been signed on other side; maybe it's -- it's the order of the 13th of -- of August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you -- can you see that by this letter General Hadzihasanovic is basically saying, "I cannot take them on. I don't want to open a third front. And please send me another order." Is that the gist of this document?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could interpret this this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That would be a reasonable interpretation.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we look at the next document, General, this is the one where we have -- called "Authorisation." This is also a document that has been provided to you.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that's just what I just was talking and referring to before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this document authorised a Mr. Mahmuljin, who is, according to this document, a member of the 3rd Corps Command, and to carry out on behalf of the army, not on behalf of the 3rd Corps, negotiations and arrangements with the representatives of the Mujahedin. And they say -- it appears to be from Zenica. And the two things they want to negotiate upon is the inclusion of the Mujahedin into the army and the use of that unit against a fight against the Chetniks. And, as it says: "The manner of his resubordination." Can you confirm that this letter confirms that as of that date, the 23rd of July, this unit has not been resubordinated to the 3rd Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that, of course, the order is -- is issued with the idea to solve this problem. You would agree that this is a problem?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the problem. This is the reason why the 3rd Corps commander addressed his higher headquarters about this problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I put it to you that Mr. Mahmuljin, albeit that it says here that he was a member of the 3rd Corps Command -- Sorry, General, I have to go back to my previous question in terms of whether this would be a reasonable interpretation that General Hadzihasanovic was saying, "I cannot take them on and please send me a new order." And your answer was not recorded on the transcript. Can you confirm that what your answer was in terms of whether this interpretation was a reasonable interpretation.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said this is a -- this is a possible way to interpret it this way, because there's still a question mark.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I added then, "Was it reasonable?"

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your answer was --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this authorisation, if I put it to you that Mr. Mahmuljin was not a member of the 3rd Corps, despite what it says here, would that show you again to say that there is something going on again between someone higher than the 3rd Corps but that's something to which General Hadzihasanovic is not privy to?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: But how should I know that he is not a member of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just suggest to you. Now, General, can you see on this letter or authorisation, can you see that this authorisation has not been sent or has not been copied to General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't show.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would that also indicate that what is going on is beyond the reach of the knowledge of General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't -- I wouldn't deduct this from what you just said. It's a personal authorisation for that gentleman, which he needs to go to the Mujahedin in order to authorise his capability to negotiate with them; therefore, it doesn't have to be -- it hasn't been issued to General Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- but would you say -- would you agree with me that the fact that this letter was not copied to General Hadzihasanovic, when we are talking about a very important problem that he raised in the first place that, as a minimum, he should be informed about someone being nominated to go and negotiate with these people?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- I understand it this way: If this gentleman was from the 3rd Corps - and I assume he was from the 3rd Corps - there's no question that the corps commander was informed about that, especially since the corps commander raised this issue as a key issue on his behalf. Even if I have not the paper on that, it doesn't say it hasn't happened. So I assume, seeing the cooperation between the higher headquarter and General Hadzihasanovic on a daily basis that he very well knew about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if I look at the next document - and I have to move quickly, because we're a bit short on time - there is a proposal dated the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this is dated -- if you look at the last document, was 23rd of July and this document is the 12th of August. This is a proposal that is sent to the supreme headquarters, and the idea is, "Proposal for the formation of a detachment of foreign citizens." Would simply the title indicate to you that this detachment has not yet been created?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true. This is still a proposal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that at that time -- again, we find in the first paragraph, or the introductory paragraph that: "Given the need to organise and to make use of the foreign volunteers," would that indicate to you, General, that maybe there was an intent to say that, "Yes, we should use them because they're Muslim and maybe we can benefit from their presence but this is not taking place at this time." Would you agree with me with this interpretation?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I agree with you that the commanding general of the 3rd Corps was very interested to get this matter solved as urgently as possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this specific paragraph, General, refers to the authorisation, 129754 of 23 July. Now, what I don't understand is that this proposal here refers to a specific document which was not copied to General Hadzihasanovic. The fact that this order coming back from the corps is -- a proposal coming back from the corps is the proposal that refers to an authorisation on which it is not -- or which was not copied to the general, would that indicate to you that whoever drafted this proposal might not even have shown it to General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That might be true. It might not be true. At least, that this proposal here shows that the 3rd Corps was deeply involved in the creation of the El Mujahedin, because they even proposed a name for that. And that they have prepared the steps that in case they get the green light from higher headquarters, they could put it into being immediately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my deduction from that. It shows that the corps is very well involved in the process of getting this problem resolved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they want -- and you can see from this that General Hadzihasanovic, at least from the time he wrote this letter to this time, that he is actively involved in solving this issue, in solving this issue without having to fight the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it's amazing that it took until now two months already from his initial proposal until the realisation, so it shows it was a very cumbersome and difficult process to achieve.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, General, recently you did an interview concerning the -- what the situation in Iraq, with respect to the United States. And you were referring in that interview that to solve problems such as these with the independent units, that the use of force should not be the way to go but, rather, we should do it by finding a political solution to problems like this and to get those people in Iraq under and to create [sic]. Would you say that on the basis of your own opinion that what General Hadzihasanovic was doing and not to take them on and, rather, to find the proper solution with the help of a superior headquarters was the reasonable thing to do for General Hadzihasanovic to focus on his mission?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has been talking before about the third front, and maybe this was -- and we know from the documents how difficult it was to deal with the Mujahedin, that they were very trigger happy in their way to do business, and this is maybe the reason why he hasn't done anything beforehand. But by that time, when he initiated, what we were just discussing the last 10 minutes or 14 minutes, I'm absolutely with you. But let me also refer that Delic told them, "If they don't comply, show them the hospitality and disarm them." So Delic was willing to take them on and say, "I'm not willing to continue what they have done until now." And the question for me is not whether he -- what he has done right now is the appropriate way. I think there's absolutely no question about this. The question is whether he should have done a little bit earlier things like this in order not to establish a third front but to disarm the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what you say, General, in your opinion, of course, is that -- and that is also in your report, that until the next piece of paper, which is what we have here on the 13th of August -- and this 13th of August we have the formation of a detachment is being created. And we talk about this thing called El Mujahed Detachment in the 3 Corps zone of responsibility. And a number is given. Now, this is, of course -- this task is to be realised immediately, and that is done on the 13th of August.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from the documents that have been shown to you, you have no way of saying when exactly, if ever, this order was activated.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my understanding of an order like this, once it's been published, it's activated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I hereby order." So why should I activate it any more if I have ordered it, for me as a commanding general or the chief of the army, in this -- of the armed forces by that time, once I order it, it goes out and we will execute it. Why should I do something else on -- on that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, would you agree with me that if General Hadzihasanovic wanted to organise or to accomplish and execute this order, that it would be important for a reasonable commander to try and find where the leadership was, find who the members of that unit are, find out where they are, and to ensure that anything would be done the proper way?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that if there was going to be any unit like this, that its commander, in accordance with the rules of regulation that you have seen, would have to be appointed by Izetbegovic himself and by no one else.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether Izetbegovic appointed every battalion commander; maybe he did. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that's the law that was -- in the documents, in the material that were given to you, any -- any appointment -- assignment of battalion commanders and up had to be done by --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- had to be done by the -- by the Presidency, upon recommendation of the Minister of National Defence.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That being the case, he probably -- not probably. Then he had appointed this commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this order, of course, if on paper we've created this entity, until we have a commander assigned officially by the Presidency and until we have actually something done physically, then we can't say that this unit exists as of yet?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This unit existed because we know where they were stationed, we know where they trained, we know -- and if I look again into the video, I would know who was the commander by that time, because they are very clear who was when the commander. But I don't have any document on that. And it doesn't say, since this is the only document which I have, that this commander could not have been appointed the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we look into the fact that your last answer, the fact that take away the video that you have, you don't know where they trained and you don't know where they are and the leadership is not accessible, as is pointed out in your report; am I correct in saying that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because I think also from other sources, sources from the 7th Mountain Brigade, we know that Mehurici -- Mehurici was one of the training areas in which they lived. We also know about other places where they were working. So it was not -- it was not a shadow force for the Bosnian army. They knew where they were. They knew where their commanders were. Otherwise, I think the reaction of the commanding general of the 3rd Corps to get them organised -- and also, as we have seen, he asked -- they have asked them before to join the Bosnian army, because it was rejected by the Mujahedin, so there was a connection -- a connection with them. I think your deductions are just not deductions I would like to take.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, if I move on with the next document that you have, in terms of an order which has got the signature block of the general, but then there is a mention about the subordination of this apparently independent detachment El Mujahed, and this order is to the -- addressed to the commander of the 306th Brigade, but there is the mention there: "Not carried out." Is there a possibility, simply a possibility that this order was not carried out on the order of General Hadzihasanovic himself?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Might be. But why -- why do you write an order if you don't carry it out afterwards?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- but there could be many reasons why this could take place. Did you -- did you, General, have in your whole career, have had to issue orders that then you've had to take back or cancel for various reasons?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of. Maybe I did, but I -- I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, if we look at the last document that you have in this pile of documents, dating back to 21 of February, 1994. And can you look at this document and read the first paragraph, because this document was not given to you.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this -- would you agree with me on the basis of the fourth line that this was -- relates to a conversation between a man called Abu Haris, who appears to be a commander of the -- appears to be, at least based on this document, a conversation with the commander of the army, and that is in February of 1994, and this is that people who are on this list no longer want to be working with the Mujahedin and that all the Mujahedin don't want to give their passport and their names to the 3rd Corps, even though they're being requested to do so by the chief of security?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would that also be an indication that even in 1994, the beginning of 1994, the situation with respect to the status of these foreigners was still kind of up in the air?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the status was not quite up -- up in the air, because he is -- he represents the unit of El Mujahedin. So the unit by that time must have been organised. The question is how can you control the guys in that unit, and -- and how can you make them behave as the other soldiers should behave. It seems that it was very difficult to control them, even in 1994. But I think the organisation as such is there, and if you have included them in your organisation and if they misbehave, then you take the responsibility what they have done in -- under your command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, General, if I look at the -- this specific case that we've just discussed, the creation of this so-called unit, El Mujahed, but even on the basis of the documents that you have had access to, am I right in saying that you are not in a position to confirm that there were no other elements of foreigners also present in that territory which have nothing to do with the people we are referring to here, which is the El Mujahed?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- I know not from the documents but I have read that other people were there, some kind of mercenaries, but individuals only, not as a unit as we see it here with the El Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are aware of that personally or from the documents that were given to you?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said not from the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only from what I read in -- in public sources.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there is a possibility that despite all the reasonable steps taken by General Hadzihasanovic to handle the specific problems, it might have been the end solution to the complete problem of these fighters coming from abroad within the 3rd Corps in 1993.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Might be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, General. This is the end of my cross-examination. I thank you very much for your patience and for answering all of my questions. And my colleague after the break will have some further questions for you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm aware of the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'm aware of the time. I have two questions, first relating to the packet of documents and the status -- or the Defence position with respect to these documents. This of course can be dealt with after the break. I also, Mr. President, would suggest for the record of these proceedings that the document entitled, "Hypothetical case Dusina" be somehow marked or attached to these proceedings, because the witness made several references to this document during the cross-examination. I'm not proposing that it be admitted into evidence but perhaps it could be marked or made a court exhibit for purposes of maintaining a copy of this document in the court proceedings. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Regarding the documents, there are two questions: First of all, you gave us two binders with documents, appear to be official documents, as they are military orders in most cases. These documents were not in the possession of the witness or the Prosecution. Could you tell us where did you get those documents from? We know that the Prosecution seized in Sarajevo a certain number of documents. They seized the originals. Does this mean that you or members of your team went to the Sarajevo archives, looked through the documents, and asked for photocopies of the originals, and you were given copies of those documents? Under what legal format did you obtain them? How did you obtain access to the official archives? So would you explain to us how you managed to get hold of these documents and is there any trace of the fact that the documents were given to you officially? Because there should be a stamp of the Sarajevo archives on a document saying that they were given to so and so. So, Madam Residovic, can you explain the source of the documents in the two binders?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Some of the documents have Prosecution numbers on them, and they were disclosed to us under the disclosure procedure. That is clearly indicated on each of the documents that we received in the pre-trial stage.
