In accordance with the Statute of this Tribunal and the Rules of Procedure and the agreement on cooperation between the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the International Tribunal, at the very beginning of these proceedings, after our client had his Initial Appearance in the Tribunal, the Defence of General Hadzihasanovic, as well as General Kubura's defence, addressed the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the basis of the equality of arms that we should be allowed access to the archives of the state and other archives. The government of Bosnia and Herzegovina passed conclusions instructing the state authorities to provide the investigators of both teams with access to those archives. On the basis of this, the Defence has managed to gain access to the state archives, first the army archives, then the archives of the Defence Ministry of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the archives of the police, the courts, the prosecutor's offices, and all the documents in the binders given to you which do not come from the Prosecution are the result of our own investigations during the pre-trial proceedings. The Defence, again in accordance with the cooperation between the Republic of Croatia and this Tribunal, the Defence addressed the liaison office of Croatia to allow us access to the state archives of Croatia containing the HVO documents. We were given that permission, and we were disclosed a number of reports from the presidential archives of the Republic of Croatia, and through official communication with the UN we were enabled to have access to UNPROFOR archives in Geneva. Through direct contacts with the responsible authorities of Great Britain, we were given access to the documents of the British Battalion; and you're also familiar with the measures taken by the Defence teams to get access to the archives of the European monitors. So those would be the sources of the documents that will be presented to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am grateful for this information indicating the origin and sources of the documents that you have shown the witness. There is a series of documents whose fate hasn't been regulated. First of all, the document that was given to General Reinhardt through the Victims and Witnesses Unit are the documents that he has reviewed; therein the documents on the hypothetical, the Dusina case, questions, and the table. Are you asking for these documents to be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The only document that I referred to today was the document on Dusina that my learned friend referred to. While preparing the cross-examination, I noticed that unfortunately I don't have time to use the documents in the way I intended to do. I really would have preferred to have been able to have more time for the cross-examination of this witness and to show him each of the documents in turn. But we tried to speed things up, and therefore that was not possible, so I focussed only on one case today; that is, the case of Dusina. Therefore, regarding all the other documents, they should be put aside; whereas, the Dusina document could be marked for identification or even tendered into evidence, if my learned friend has no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, regarding the Dusina document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Dusina document was the only one I made reference to earlier. We would certainly support it being marked for identification or being attached as some kind of a court exhibit. We would oppose it being admitted into evidence on the ground that we've litigated the issue of these facts, and we would simply ask that it be somehow attached to the record so that in the event of any appellant proceedings and a review of the transcript where the witness is making reference to this document, that it be available to the Appeals Chamber to review this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let us give it an ID number. Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it will have DH number 164 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Now, we have another document, a set of documents shown to the witness, and within this set, there are documents which are already a part of the court file and then there are also new documents; specifically documents which appear for the first time, specifically the one of the 21st of February, 1994. Is the Defence asking us to give one number for all these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think an ID number for this set, and then we will consult with the Prosecution to see what the positions of the parties are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. Mr. Mundis agrees. Can we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH165 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now, we still have outstanding the problem of the maps. What is the Defence going to tell us about this large board with the maps? Are you going to ask that they be tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my idea was to have photographs focussed on by the camera in the courtroom or even to use a digital camera. However, in view of the actual use I made of the map, we will produce the UN map and General Hadzihasanovic's map later on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It is 12.30. We will resume at five to 1.00, and then it will be the turn of the other Defence team, that is, Mr. Dixon, who will have one hour at his disposal, maybe a few minutes more, to allow him to cross-examine the witness. So we will resume at five to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Bourgon, you have concluded your cross-examination. I will give Mr. Dixon the floor now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: May it please Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Dixon:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Reinhardt, it may be trite, but it is correct, is it not, that a commander may only be held responsible for the perpetrators of war crimes if those perpetrators are indeed his subordinates within his chain of command?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yep.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the perpetrators are not the subordinates of the commander, then the issue of notice is wholly irrelevant; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- I would not say "wholly irrelevant." Because I think nevertheless you are responsible what happens in the area. And if there are fighters in the area which cooperate and coordinate their activities with you, you take over responsibility of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would you agree with me that unless those people are under your command, then you can't be held responsible for their actions. If they are under the command of somebody else, then it's that person who's responsible?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the -- basically I'm absolutely with you. And the question is: What does it mean, "under your command"? If I plan an operation, a military operation, and execute this military operation with people who are executing this together with me, for these -- these elements, then, are under my command for the purpose of this particular operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, because you have effective control over them.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's why you have responsibility for them.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Even so, they don't belong to your own organic organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking in general terms, General Reinhardt, not about the --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- scenario you're outlining. The basic principle is they must be your subordinates before you can be held responsible.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if they're not your subordinates, it doesn't matter whether you got information or not about what was going on with those perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also, it doesn't matter if you took no actions in respect of those perpetrators, if they're not your subordinates.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we turn to Vares. That was an area where you in your report at paragraph 9.5.2 were somewhat critical of my client --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We would all agree that there were units of the 7th Brigade in Vares in November 1993; they were there with a number of other units and brigades conducting an operation. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, an organisational group had been formed, call the OG Istok.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the 7th Brigade units were part of that, together with a number of other units.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your report, you say that: "On 4 November 1993 the commander of the 306th Brigade reported criminal activities of the 7th Brigade soldiers during the operations against Vares."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you go on to say that you would have expected Mr. Kubura to look further into those reports and not just accept the report of the commander of his second battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where you said there was a report from the 306th Brigade in the first sentence, there's no footnote there indicating what document you rely upon, is there?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I think I can -- I can tell you what document it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If you could, because what I'm trying to establish is what report was sent and indeed whether Mr. Kubura got that report.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know which report we are talking about offhand, or would you need to go through the documents in --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- some detail?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I -- maybe you'd give me a chance to go through the documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I can assist in the interests of time. Is it not correct - and I can show you these documents, if you wish - that in fact the 306th Brigade was never in Vares; it operated in Travnik? And we are talking here about reports from the OG Istok that I referred to earlier on, two reports; one on the 4th of November, 1993, and second on the 4th of November, 1993. These are documents which you have received. You might not have them with you, I appreciate, because they weren't referred to in your report. They are PT116 and PT827. My point is, General Reinhardt, that -- and you can look at them, if you wish, but it might be quicker if we just go through it with me --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- leading you -- that both of these reports were sent by the commander of the operational group directly to the 3rd Corps Command and the 6th Corps Command. There was no copy sent to Mr. Kubura. He wasn't even given a cc'd copy for information.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You would accept that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, if you say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: The document, Your Honours, are two contested exhibits, 46 and 306.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course, General, these are documents that are not in evidence yet.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Fortunately this is a matter that doesn't have to concern you, whether or not they are to be admitted. But these are documents which you did have and which you would have been able to review in drawing up your report.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree, then, that it would not be correct to say that Mr. Kubura should have followed up those reports if he didn't receive them?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was entitled to rely on the report of the commander of his 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we move on to Kakanj, then, which was another incident that you mentioned. For the record - you may or may not know this - but the looting in that area is not in fact charged in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is -- sorry, General.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just took that case not because of what happened but how General Hadzihasanovic reacted, saying this was a very good way how to solve and react to a course, which -- to a case which has been presented to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And you said also in your -- your evidence-in-chief, and this is while asking you about it, that you weren't sure that action was followed up by the brigade commander further down the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a document which you may have in front of you, another contested exhibit. This is a document that you were given, and it's PT538 -- PTW538. It's a letter from General Hadzihasanovic to the Supreme Command, and it says --

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: And perhaps it might be best, Your Honours, if General Reinhardt is given a copy.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Of this. Otherwise, we'll spend so much time going through various pages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a document you recall looking at? It was in the bundle that was given to you.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be that I have seen that. I don't -- I don't recall it right now. Maybe I -- it just didn't come to my attention. If you say I have been issued this, it might be true, but I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Otherwise, my conclusion would have been different.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General, if I could refer you to the second-last paragraph. It's a simple point which I wish you to confirm.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is that it reads: "Pursuant to the order of the 7th Brigade Command a battalion commander, company commander, and several other 7th Battalion officers were relieved of their duties in Kakanj on 23 June 1993 for failing to carry out an order to prevent crime and looting." Would you agree that that order indicates that on its face the matter was followed up and these persons were removed from their duties by the 7th Brigade Command?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you also agree that having looked at a number of additional documents this morning about measures taken, that this might not be the only incident where action was taken and followed up all the way down to the brigade level?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having seen these additional documents, I already reversed my -- my position this morning, because I haven't had more by the time when I was looking into the case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this would apply both to the 3rd Corps Command and also further down the chain of command to the brigade commands as well.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not be ad libitum in this regard because I don't know exactly what the brigade commander has done in that case. I haven't seen any reliable actions. But if you say so, I must -- I must assume that you have better evidence than I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not going to burden you with files of more documents. My point only is that you weren't given all of the material that could be applicable in this case. You were given as much as was necessary, which you've reviewed, but there is additional material which you haven't reviewed.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was, and I see there is additional material I haven't reviewed and which haven't had impact on my statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Turning to Miletici, then. Is it correct that there were no 7th Brigade personnel deployed in Miletici in April 1993?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to Maljine. Is it correct that likewise there were no 7th Brigade personnel committed to the fighting in Maljine?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it correct from all the material that you've been --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I see the material, yes, this is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a document which was given to you, another one which you probably don't have, because it wasn't one referred to in your report. This is an uncontested exhibit, so it's got an exhibit number already, Exhibit P174. And for you, General, it would be PT108. If you could be given a copy of it, as I don't think you --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- you have it in front of you.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a report dated 21 October 1993 from the deputy commander of the 3rd Corps going to the Supreme Command Staff; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall seeing this --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- document? I can confirm that it was given to you, but it may be amongst all the documents. It's entirely understandable that you cannot remember each individual one. Can you confirm, however, by looking at the document now that in this report the deputy commander is reporting on the incident that occurred in Maljine in October 1993 [sic], and nowhere is it indicated that any members of the 7th Brigade were deployed there?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a translation on the front of it, the English translation you're working from.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the -- the back of it, there's a copy of the original document in B/C/S. I just wish to clarify one point, and that regards -- and that's regarding the translation of the document. As I say, this is not -- this is not a contested document. And that is that in paragraph 2 it says: "Where soldiers of the --" and it says: "illegible" and no brigade number is filled in. If you look at the original, from what I can see it's quite clear that it reads: "306th Brigade." Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll just try to find out, please. Give me ... Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it reads: "306 Brigade."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be: "306 Brigade," yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it goes on to say: "Armed citizens who were not members of the BH army units."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: There's one correction to the transcript, Your Honour, and that is that the date for Maljine that's at line 23 is not October 1993 -- it's page 100, line 23 -- but in fact, October 1993 is mentioned there. It should be June 1993. The document is dated October 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General. If you could move on now to paragraph 4.5 of your report. My learned friend from the Prosecution took you to that paragraph earlier on, where you say that: "Based on the material I have looked through, it is not quite clear to me to which extent and under what kind of command relationship elements of the Mujahedin were fighting within the 7th Brigade before they were officially recognised into an independent 3rd Corps detachment on 13 August 1993." That your -- that is your conclusion, is it?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said in your evidence in chief that there was no clear order that says that the Mujahedin or a group of them belonged to the 7th Brigade. You couldn't find any such document.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that the documents that you reviewed some -- some 400 documents - you said this in your evidence in chief; I just wish to confirm it - that they did not give a very clear indication, that you could only make deductions and assumptions.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. I can make deductions and assumptions from documents which I have looked through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: But as assumptions and deductions are not a clear 100 per cent evidence, it is only that I can take some logical consequences out of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are interpreting the documents, a process which you would agree anyone in the courtroom can undertake, making deductions and assumptions from documents which are not very clear.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The video was mentioned earlier on. I'm quite clear that this was not the only material that you based your conclusion on. There were documents and the video. But for your benefit and the benefit obviously of Their Honours, I wish to play you the portion of the video which you referred to in your report.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are many portions, quite a few portions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. There's one particular portion, if I may indicate which that is, and that is the one referred to in paragraph 4.6, the paragraph just after the one I've referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Perhaps we should clarify that first, and then we will -- we will show the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 4.6: "According to the videotape, somewhere in early 1992 an agreement was made with the commander of the Muslim forces in Travnik to send a group of his best soldiers to join the ranks of the Mujahedin and train them to carry out special operations."

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is a quote from the written transcript --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- which you had.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you've confirmed, you never looked at the video; you simply read the transcript.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. But I have to say in the footnote it shows that "1992" must be "1993." I said this correctly in the footnote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So when you say: "In early 1992" --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It must be 1993, as it says in the footnote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, so it's 1993 we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a typing error.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Okay. If we could show, with the leave of Your Honours, the portion of the video. It is a very short portion. And we -- we might need to show it twice in order that it can be fully appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would suggest that we show it one further time, as it is very short. Unfortunately, the sound cannot be increased. The words that are heard spoken in the background are those that appear in the transcript. But the purpose of showing the video was to ask General Reinhardt to comment on what in fact he sees now on the video. So it could be shown again, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Reinhardt, having now seen the video, would you agree with me now that there's nothing in the video material which indicates who the soldiers are?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's nothing in the material which indicates that they are soldiers of the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or that the commander that may have indicated that there should be training was a commander of the 7th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say anything about the 7th Brigade in this regard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, would you agree that, having seen the video, that material could have been taken at any time and be of any troops?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not -- it's not necessary that the -- that the text of the video and the -- and the picture which we have seen, the movie which we have seen, are -- are coincidental?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And yet, you have said in your report and in your evidence in chief that it says very clearly - we're talking about the video here - that, "They offered training" - this is the Mujahedin - "to the battalion, to one of the battalions of the 7th Mountain Brigade." And I think training is part of cooperation.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Leaving your assumptions aside, you would agree that the hard evidence does not show that that is the 7th Brigade there offering the training.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I deducted, as you can see from my footnote --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- he's talking about the command of the Muslim forces in Travnik, and this was the 1st Battalion being stationed in Travnik, that him being the commander, one could deduct that this is then the one he was negotiating with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's footnote 57 that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's a deduction that you make on the basis that the 7th Brigade had a battalion in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are aware that there were many other brigades and units based in Travnik, are you not?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So would you agree that it's possible that when forces are referred to, it could be referring to other units and not the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be also other units. I could not exclude this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on the video material and the documents that you refer to in your report, your conclusion on this topic is set out in paragraph 4.11 of your report, is it not, where you say: "Based on the scarce information --" so you would regard the information as limited; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "From existing documents, one can assume that at least certain elements of the Mujahedin were incorporated in the organisation of the 7th Brigade battalions, beginning in early 1993." Would I be correct in saying, as you mentioned earlier on, that a logical extension of this conclusion is that there were elements that were not incorporated in the 7th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you cannot say which elements were in and which --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- elements were out?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot. Therefore, I leave it so dubious, because it remained dubious for me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It remained blurred, as you said.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have, in respect of the Mujahedin, indicated that from the evidence that you've looked at they came to fight for a Jihad in 1992.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They arrived before the BH army was organised into corps and battalions.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you've also said that they were not very happy with their situation. They were disillusioned because the Bosnians did not share the same aims or mission as them.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they thought they were professionally not well trained enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And that they also, you said in your evidence in chief, wanted to be in a unit in the Bosnian army, under a direct chain of command.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They wanted to be as a unit in the direct chain of command, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are aware that they had their own independent funding from abroad?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you've indicated in your evidence so far, these factors led to the development in August 1993 towards the building up of a organic unit of the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is true. And coming back to the last question, they had their organic funding but they were also issued weapons by the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even so they had their organic funding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They had funding to buy their own weapons, did they not?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said in your evidence in chief that there was no document before August of 1993 from which you could deduct that there were foreigners part of a unit of the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They wanted to become a defined unit.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is what began occurring, in your view, from August onwards.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: From June onwards. Because this is when General Hadzihasanovic sent his request to higher headquarters to have this problem solved, so it's not only the end which we are talking about. We have to see that this was an evolutionary development.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You haven't seen any orders from Mr. Kubura in respect of this process, have you?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would it be correct to say that before this process began they were an independent grouping, they were not within a unit in the Bosnian army, and that the entire process that you've outlined was an effort, a difficult one, but an effort to slowly bring them within the army over time?

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was slowly an effort to bring them in the army over time and to regulate the kind of cooperation which have developed in the meantime in the appropriate channels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You cannot say, though, from the documents when this process was completed.

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the process was completed by the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment, because then they become a unit, an official unit of the Bosnian-Herzegovinian army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm referring to, General, is the process was completed in terms of bringing all these elements fully within the command structures of the Bosnian army. That took some time --

utterances.speaker: KLAUS REINHARDT [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it started by that time. And since this was a rather loose group of people, these El Mujahedin, I don't know when it really stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I have no further questions on behalf of Mr. Kubura. And, Your Honours, there are no documents to -- to tender, as these documents are either exhibits already or they are contested exhibits, and that will have to be resolved through -- through the arguments that are ongoing before Your Honours. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dixon. The Trial Chamber notes today at 1.30 that the cross-examination of this witness conducted by the Defence has now been concluded. Tomorrow will be used for re-examination on the part of the Prosecution and for the Judges' questions. At this point in time, would it be possible for the Prosecution to inform us of the amount of time they will require for the additional questions they will be putting to the witness in the light of the witness's cross-examination that concerned a number of subjects. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Based on the guidance that we had received from the Trial Chamber earlier, the Prosecution was of the view that the questions from the Trial Chamber would be the next item or the next order of business. Am I mistaken in that respect, Mr. President? I had assumed, in other words, that Your Honours would have questions and then we would return, if there's time remaining, to the parties for any questions, based on questions from Your Honours as well as the cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber would prefer the Prosecution to commence with its re-examination now that the cross-examination has been concluded. You could put questions with regard to the report of the witness and the items -- the items that have been contested by the Defence. We could thus dispose of this matter, and the Judges could then ask the witness questions. We will soon have to adjourn, so if you are not prepared to commence now, we can start tomorrow. You could start with your re-examination tomorrow, unless there aren't any questions that you have to put to the witness. That is also a possibility. The Judges will then ask the witness some questions about the report and various other elements that arose in the course of the cross-examination. Mr. Mundis, would you prefer to wait until tomorrow in order to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution would indeed prefer to re-examine the witness tomorrow. With respect to timing, the Prosecution will certainly take no more than one hour for re-examination, and there is, of course, a possibility that the Prosecution will have only a few questions in re-examination. There has obviously been a large amount of material that's been covered on cross-examination, and we would like the opportunity for the remainder of today to review that. But certainly we will take no more than one hour, and I would -- I would hazard to guess that it would be substantially less than one hour. We're certainly aware that Your Honours have questions, and obviously those questions -- we don't want to run out of time, take too much time that Your Honours would have questions. But I don't anticipate that we would have much, and certainly no more than one hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You plan to re-examine the witness for about an hour. The Judges will then have some questions. And the Defence would like to ask some other questions. The witness might be able to go home earlier than we thought tomorrow. But in any case, the hearing should be concluded by 1.45 tomorrow. Nevertheless, it's possible that you might be able to leave at an earlier time; that depends on the questions that will be put to you by the parties involved. We will now adjourn. And I would like to invite everyone to be present for the hearing that will commence tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
